sentences.en: Friar Lawrence’s Cell
sentences.ko: 로런스 신부의 수도실

summary.en: Romeo and Juliet meet at Friar Lawrence's cell, and he marries them in secret.
summary.ko: 로미오와 줄리엣이 로런스 신부의 수도실에서 만나고, 신부는 두 사람을 몰래 결혼시킨다.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
So smile the heavens upon this holy act
That after-hours with sorrow chide us not.

sentences.en: May heaven smile on this holy act.
sentences.ko: 하늘이 이 거룩한 예식에 미소 지어 주시길.

sentences.en: May it not cause us sorrow later.
sentences.ko: 훗날 슬픔으로 우리를 꾸짖지 않으시길.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Amen, amen, but come what sorrow can,
It cannot countervail the exchange of joy
That one short minute gives me in her sight.
Do thou but close our hands with holy words,
Then love-devouring death do what he dare,
It is enough I may but call her mine.

sentences.en: Amen, amen.
sentences.ko: 아멘, 아멘.

sentences.en: Whatever sorrow may come, it cannot outweigh the joy that one short minute with her gives me.
sentences.ko: 어떤 슬픔이 와도, 그녀와 함께하는 짧은 1분의 기쁨보다 클 수는 없어요.

sentences.en: Just join our hands with holy words.
sentences.ko: 성스러운 말로 우리의 손을 묶어주세요.

sentences.en: Then let death do what it dares.
sentences.ko: 그다음엔 죽음이 무슨 짓을 하든 상관없어요.

sentences.en: It is enough that I can call her mine.
sentences.ko: 그녀를 내 사람이라 부를 수 있다는 것만으로도 충분해요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
These violent delights have violent ends,
And in their triumph die; like fire and powder,
Which as they kiss consume. The sweetest honey
Is loathsome in his own deliciousness,
And in the taste confounds the appetite.
Therefore love moderately: long love doth so;
Too swift arrives as tardy as too slow.

sentences.en: These violent delights have violent ends and die in their triumph.
sentences.ko: 격렬한 기쁨은 격렬한 결말을 맞이하고 승리의 순간에 사라진다.

sentences.en: They are like fire and gunpowder, which explode as they kiss.
sentences.ko: 그것들은 입맞추는 순간 터져 버리는 불과 화약 같다.

sentences.en: Even the sweetest honey becomes sickening when you have too much.
sentences.ko: 가장 달콤한 꿀이라도 너무 많이 먹으면 역겨워지는 법이다.

sentences.en: Its taste ruins the appetite, so love moderately.
sentences.ko: 그 맛은 식욕을 망치니, 사랑도 적당히 해야 한다.

sentences.en: That is how love lasts.
sentences.ko: 그래야 사랑이 오래 지속된다.

sentences.en: Going too fast gets you there as late as going too slow.
sentences.ko: 너무 빨리 서두르는 것은 너무 느리게 가는 것만큼이나 늦게 도착하게 만든다.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Here comes the lady. O, so light a foot
Will ne’er wear out the everlasting flint.
A lover may bestride the gossamers
That idles in the wanton summer air
And yet not fall; so light is vanity.

sentences.en: Here comes the lady.
sentences.ko: 아가씨가 오는구나.

sentences.en: Her step is so light it would never wear down the hard stone path.
sentences.ko: 그녀의 발걸음은 매우 가벼워 딱딱한 돌길을 전혀 닳게 하지 않는다.

sentences.en: A lover could walk on the spider threads that float in the summer air and not fall.
sentences.ko: 연인은 여름 공중에 떠다니는 거미줄 위를 걸어도 떨어지지 않을 것이다.

sentences.en: Earthly joy is that light.
sentences.ko: 세상의 기쁨이란 그렇게 가벼운 것이다.

speaker: JULIET
raw: Good even to my ghostly confessor.

sentences.en: Good evening, Father.
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 신부님.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw: Romeo shall thank thee, daughter, for us both.

sentences.en: Romeo will thank you, daughter, for both of us.
sentences.ko: 딸아, 로미오가 우리 둘 몫까지 네게 인사할 게다.

speaker: JULIET
raw: As much to him, else is his thanks too much.

sentences.en: Then I give him the same thanks, or his thanks would be too much.
sentences.ko: 그럼 저도 로미오에게 똑같이 인사해야죠. 안 그러면 그의 인사가 과분하니까요.

speaker: ROMEO
raw:
Ah, Juliet, if the measure of thy joy
Be heap’d like mine, and that thy skill be more
To blazon it, then sweeten with thy breath
This neighbour air, and let rich music’s tongue
Unfold the imagin’d happiness that both
Receive in either by this dear encounter.

sentences.en: Ah, Juliet.
sentences.ko: 아, 줄리엣.

sentences.en: Your joy may be as great as mine, and you may be better at showing it.
sentences.ko: 당신의 기쁨도 나만큼 크고, 표현하는 솜씨는 더 좋을 거예요.

sentences.en: Then sweeten this air with your breath.
sentences.ko: 그럼 당신의 숨결로 이 공기를 달콤하게 채워주세요.

sentences.en: Let the music of rich words tell our story.
sentences.ko: 아름다운 말들의 선율이 우리의 이야기를 들려주게 하세요.

sentences.en: Let it show the happiness we both feel from this dear meeting.
sentences.ko: 이 소중한 만남에서 우리 둘이 느끼는 행복을 보여주세요.

speaker: JULIET
raw:
Conceit more rich in matter than in words,
Brags of his substance, not of ornament.
They are but beggars that can count their worth;
But my true love is grown to such excess,
I cannot sum up sum of half my wealth.

sentences.en: My feelings are richer in meaning than in words.
sentences.ko: 제 감정은 화려한 말보다 더 깊은 의미를 담고 있어요.

sentences.en: They show my true feelings instead of just using fancy words.
sentences.ko: 그저 멋진 말을 쓰는 대신 제 진심을 보여주는 것이니까요.

sentences.en: Only beggars can count how much they have.
sentences.ko: 자기 재산을 셀 수 있는 사람은 거지뿐이에요.

sentences.en: But my true love has grown so rich that I cannot count even half of my wealth.
sentences.ko: 하지만 내 진실한 사랑은 너무 커져서, 그 절반도 셀 수 없어요.

speaker: FRIAR LAWRENCE
raw:
Come, come with me, and we will make short work,
For, by your leaves, you shall not stay alone
Till holy church incorporate two in one.

sentences.en: Come with me now.
sentences.ko: 이제 나를 따라와라.

sentences.en: We will finish this quickly.
sentences.ko: 이 일을 빨리 끝내도록 하자.

sentences.en: You will not be left alone together until the church joins you two as one.
sentences.ko: 교회가 너희 둘을 하나로 맺어 줄 때까지 너희끼리만 두지는 않겠다.
